author: Mary Wollstonecraft
title: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
edition: Boston: printed by Peter Edes for Thomas and Andrews, 1792 (MDCCXCII on the title page). Scan-backed Wikisource transcription. Prose line wrapping is collapsed within retained paragraphs; HTML emphasis becomes plain text. Printed page numbers, navigation, footnote reference markers, and zero-width page-boundary characters are omitted; main-text wording and punctuation are retained. Original verse line breaks are preserved where present. Apparent errors present in the linked transcription are retained rather than silently corrected; this extraction check is not a fresh complete print-image collation. The library text holds the dedication to Talleyrand-Périgord, the Introduction and Chapters I to XIII with their printed chapter, part and section headings; the title page and contents are omitted; the author's seventy-five footnotes are kept, each anchor as [n] in the transcription's numbering, which restarts in each chapter, and each note as a paragraph [Footnote n: text] after its chapter's text, where the Wikisource transcription lists them. Rule lines are left out; the rows of spaced points in Chapter V are kept as paragraphs. The dedication's address and first eleven paragraphs (blocks 0–13), read as a Grade 12 holiday night, were collated on 2026-11-18 against the OCR of Internet Archive vindicationofrig00wol, this Boston printing, and against its page images for pages v–vii and x: two transcription errors were corrected to the print (“to you—the first dedication”, where the dash had slipped after “the”, and “will ever shew”, which had been modernised to “show”); long s and the flattened emphasis (“force”, “prudish”) stand as described above.

rights.basis: This original English edition was published in 1792, before 1931, and is public domain in the United States as of 2026. The linked scan index identifies the printed edition; no modern editorial material is supplied.

acquisition.method: Wikisource rendered page HTML (index.php action=render) for the fifteen subpages in printed order: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman/Dedication, /Introduction and /Chapter I to /Chapter XIII (revisions 7347881, 7347877, 7347882, 7347326, 7347325, 7347324, 7347323, 7346277, 7346261, 7347320, 7353640, 7347884, 7347885, 7357171, 7359631); downloadSha256 is the SHA-256 of the fifteen responses concatenated in that order and downloadUrl the first of them. Only the transcluded scan text is used: Wikisource headers, page-number anchors, gap spacers and zero-width page-boundary characters removed; chapter, part and section headings and centred chapter titles became headings (the three-line half-title before Chapter I joined as one); centred verse quotations became stanza blocks, one line per line break; other paragraphs joined with whitespace collapsed; emphasis flattened; footnote calls kept as [n] in Wikisource's per-subpage numbering, attached to the word before them; each subpage's reference list, which the transcription prints after the subpage's text, became one paragraph per note in Project Gutenberg's form [Footnote n: text], its paragraphs and line breaks joined with single spaces (a note that runs on from one scan page to the next is one note, its continuation marker dropped). Blocks 4 and 13 were corrected to the print on 2026-11-18 (see edition).
